title: Pilot readout and integration pathways (ACME trial)
summary: Executive readout from the 6-week ACME pilot. Demonstrates feasibility of integrating Redwood-hosted API + Dedicated fallback for peak loads. Includes technical findings, three recommended deployment pathways, cost and staffing estimates, and a prioritized next-steps checklist for product and infra owners.
key_metrics: p50 latency (hosted): 120ms; p95: 420ms. Dedicated baseline throughput: 38 reqs/sec (single GPU pool). Token cost delta: hosted ~ $0.0026/token-equivalent vs dedicated amortized ~ $0.0019/token-equivalent at ACME's workload profile. 98.4% availability during pilot window (one planned maintenance event). KV cache hit rate improved response tokens by 27% for repeat prompts.
content:
Background:

ACME ran a focused 6-week pilot to validate a hybrid serving approach for customer-facing summarization and search-augmentation features. Goal: ensure <500ms 95th latency for interactive flows and contain per-token cost within budget. Pilot used the Redwood hosted API as the primary path with a Dedicated pool staged as a regional fallback for predictable peak throughput.

High-level outcomes:
- Product acceptance: ACME POV team signed off on output quality for the summarization model; minor prompt tuning required for edge cases (legal text).
- Performance: Hosted path achieved target latencies for median traffic; p95 spikes correlated with cold KV cache windows and long-context inputs. Dedicated pool showed stable p95 < 340ms under sustained load.
- Cost: Simulated 30-day run rates show hybrid configuration yields ~18% cost savings vs hosted-only at ACME's forecasted Q3 volume.
- Ops: Integration required two small changes to ACME's request flow (tokenization pre-check and request tagging) and a brief extension to their retry policy to support safe fallback.

Technical learnings (what mattered):
1) KV cache warmup matters: Repeated customer queries saw 20-40% latency reduction after warmup. Recommend a lightweight prefetch strategy for known query clusters (see Runbook section).
2) Batching tradeoffs: Continuous batching improved throughput but increased p95 for single-user interactive sessions. Best pattern: dynamic batch window (5–15ms) with an opt-out for low-latency routes.
3) Quantized model variants: 4-bit quantized variant reduced GPU memory by ~35% with 3–7% quality delta on rouge/bleu metrics for our workloads. Good candidate for Dedicated pool to increase packing density.
4) Prefix caching for search augmentation: Maintaining short-lived prefix caches for customer session windows cut repeated token generation by ~27%.
5) Routing policy friction: ACME's edge proxy needed two labels to make routing deterministic (region, priority). Small change, outsized reliability improvement.

Three recommended integration pathways (tradeoffs and when to pick):
A) Hosted-first, Dedicated on demand (recommended for most SMB/scale-up customers)
- Description: Continue using Redwood hosted API for steady traffic; Dedicated pool configured as fallback for spikes or when policy/regulatory rules require isolation.
- Pros: Fast time-to-value, simplified ops for ACME, minimal infra investment.
- Cons: Slightly higher unit costs for steady heavy traffic; fallback complexity in retry logic.
- Key infra notes: implement request tagging, add short retry with jitter, enable automatic model variant fallback.

B) Dedicated-primary with Hosted fallback (recommended if ACME wants consistent unit economics and control)
- Description: Route production requests to Dedicated pool, fallback to hosted during rare maintenance or burst scenarios.
- Pros: Predictable per-token economics, greater control over SLAs and data isolation.
- Cons: Requires operational ownership (capacity planning, autoscale tuning).
- Key infra notes: autoscale thresholds at 70% GPU utilization; reserve 15% burst headroom to avoid synchronous throttling.

C) Hybrid split-by-route (recommended for mixed workloads: batch embedding jobs + interactive chat)
- Description: Route long-running batch/embedding workloads to Dedicated; interactive low-latency routes to Hosted with aggressive caching.
- Pros: Best cost-performance balance for mixed workloads.
- Cons: Requires per-route policies and consistent instrumentation.
- Key infra notes: maintain separate token accounting, use route-level telemetry and cost allocation tags.

Runbook (minimum viable steps to production):
- Pre-deploy checklist (owners):
  - ACME infra: add request-level metadata (route, customer-id) — owner: ACME Platform (due: 2 weeks)
  - SE: supply sample SDK snippet + pre-tokenization helper (owner: Linh, due: 4 days)
  - SRE: create Dedicated pool template and canary rollout script (owner: Marcus, due: 1 week)
  - Security: confirm KMS key exchange and SCIM config for user-level audit logs (owner: Evelyn, due: 2 weeks)
- Deploy steps:
  1) Deploy Dedicated pool in region-us-west-2 (canary with 1 GPU) and verify throughput.
  2) Enable routing rule in test environment: hosted -> dedicated fallback enabled.
  3) Run synthetic traffic for 48 hours with production-like distribution (SE to run).
  4) Execute failover drill: simulate hosted outage and observe retry/fallback behavior.
  5) Gradually increase traffic weight to Dedicated 20% -> 50% while validating latency and cost.
- Monitoring thresholds (alerts):
  - p95 latency > 500ms for 5m -> page SRE on-call
  - KV cache hit rate < 12% for 30m -> ticket for SE to review prompt patterns
  - GPU utilization sustained > 85% for 15m -> trigger autoscale or capacity request

Cost and staffing estimate (ballpark):
- One-off integration work: ~2.5 engineering weeks (SE + ACME infra) to add tagging, retries, and tokenization helper.
- Dedicated pool setup + runbook: ~1.5 SRE weeks.
- Monthly run-rate (projected at ACME Q3 volume): Hosted-first hybrid: ~$24k/month. Dedicated-primary (amortized): ~$19.6k/month. Assumptions: 12M input tokens/month; 1.3 tokens/output ratio; 30% cache reduction.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpected model quality regressions after quantization. Mitigation: A/B test traffic lane for 2 weeks with automated eval set and rollback flag.
- Risk: Cold-cache p95 spikes during morning batch start. Mitigation: scheduled pre-warm job for heavy keys and prioritize warm-up for top N customer queries.
- Risk: Cost overruns in sustained peak. Mitigation: configure hard caps and automated notifications; implement scheduled scaling windows and pre-purchased Reserved capacity in Dedicated if warranted.

Stakeholder asks (for ACME leadership):
- Approve target SLOs and cost ceiling for next quarter (proposed: p95 < 450ms, monthly infra budget cap: $30k).
- Commit to a single integration pathway (A/B/C) by end of Q1 to prevent divergent engineering work.
- Identify product owner for post-launch quality monitoring and escalation (1 FTE recommended 0.2–0.4 capacity).

Decisions log (brief):
- 2025-02-05: Chose Hosted-first fallback topology for pilot.
- 2025-02-18: Switched to quantized variant for Dedicated canary to test packing density.
- 2025-02-25: Agreed on route-level telemetry tags and tagging format.

Appendix (links and artifacts):
- Synthetic traffic script: github.com/redwood-inference/synth-traffic/tree/acme
- Eval prompts and failing cases: confluence page (linked above)
- Sample SDK snippet (JS + Python) attached in linked PR

Next steps (prioritized with owners and ETA):
1) Fix edge-case prompts in legal summarization (owner: Diego; ETA: 7 days)
2) Finalize integration pathway decision (owner: ACME Head of Platform; ETA: 2 weeks)
3) Provision Dedicated pilot pool + run synthetic test (owner: Marcus; ETA: 10 days)
4) Implement pre-warm strategy for top-50 query clusters (owner: Linh; ETA: 3 weeks)
5) Create cost dashboard and alerting for token spend (owner: Evelyn; ETA: 2 weeks)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is a working readout. Numbers are derived from pilot telemetry and small-scale cost modeling and should be re-run against ACME's full Q3 forecast before final contract signatures.
- If ACME chooses Dedicated-primary, we should scope a 60–90 day ramp plan for capacity commitments and Reserved pricing.

Contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) — ping for clarifications or to schedule the exec readout session.
conclusion: Pilot demonstrated the hybrid architecture is viable and cost-effective for ACME's use case. Immediate value unlocks from small infra changes (tagging, pre-warm) and selecting one of the three integration pathways; recommended default is Hosted-first with Dedicated fallback to balance speed and economics. Proceed with the prioritized next-steps to move from pilot to production.
